base_rate_words: The starting fact, in plain words: of 1,217 combinations a large search promoted on October 27, 2026, only 63 reached the top grade on a same-day second look, and 564 did not replicate at all. Of the 964 that could be tested, 6.5% reached the top grade and 58.5% did not replicate. Most promoted signals are already dying at promotion. That is why this page expects fading, and why the honest question is when, not whether.

coming_round_words: The first monthly round is the November round, opening Monday, November 2, 2026. It clocks zero families. Every family below is listed as not yet clockable, with the exact missing piece named, because a family can only be clocked honestly when three things exist: its strength at promotion measured over its last 21 graded sessions, a dated past record of its strength to fit the fading pattern on, and a forward strength record that actually builds up from a running record. Today no family has all three, so nothing is staked for November and nothing below is a live prediction. The dates and calls will appear here, written to the public record on the issue day itself, for any family whose three pieces exist by then.
definitions_words: A family's strength is its average agreement score over its last 21 graded sessions, signed the way it was promoted, so strength starts positive. Its half value is half that starting strength. Fading to half means the first session the strength falls to or past that half value. Each family is counted once. A family that dies before day 60 stays in the count and counts as a hit on a yes call, never as an exit.

explanation.body: Its forecast takes this form: timing and probability, over 60 sessions, monthly cohorts. It is graded on whether its timing calls resolve by each stated horizon, with unresolved cases still counted. It would be ended if after 24 monthly cohorts, its date error is no better than predicting the family's median historical half-life for every family. It counts as proven at 24 monthly cohorts.
explanation.summary: Publish each forecaster family's expected fading date in advance, the date its strength is expected to fall to half of what it was at promotion, and stake a call on it.

idea_words: Every trading signal fades. A method that looked strong when it was picked gets weaker as the market moves on, and most fading is only ever noticed long after it happened. This page does the noticing in advance: at the start of each month it publishes, for each named group of forecasters on this site's public record, the date by which that group's strength is expected to fall to half of what it was when the group was promoted, and stakes a plain yes-or-no call on whether the halving happens within the next 60 trading days. Both are written down before the window opens and graded on day 60, exactly.
kill_words: After 24 monthly rounds, this page's expected fading dates must land closer to the real fading dates than the simple rival's (each family's own middle past fading time, predicted every month). If they do not, this page retires and its record stays up intact. That test cannot bite until both this page and the rival have real fading times to compare, and the page says so.

model_words: The fading pattern this page will use is built from a family's age since promotion, how fast its strength has been sliding and how unevenly, how far today's market sits from the market the family was found in, and how crowded its family is (how many sibling combinations share its kind of evidence). It is NOT FITTED yet, and this page says so rather than dressing up a guess: the record it would be fitted on holds no dated strength paths and not one observed fading time, so there is no fitted shape and no honest past accuracy to quote. Its past accuracy is recorded as: not measurable, because zero fading times have ever been observed here. When it is fitted, it will be fitted only on this page's own matured, graded outcomes, never on ungraded hopes.
prior_words: What the one completed life cycle does show, as a starting expectation and nothing more: pooled across all 45 forecaster-and-target pairs, 6.5% of tested combinations reached the top grade, 41.5% reached the top grade or held their direction, and 58.5% did not replicate. The strongest pair, the volatility family aiming at realised movement, saw 48 of its 83 tested combinations reach the top grade; most other pairs saw none. The full pair-by-pair counts are in the table below. These are survival counts from one recheck, not fading times, and this page never presents them as fading times.
